name: Chicago Metro Freezer Addition

hero.alt: Completed insulated metal panel freezer addition seen from the plant yard under an overcast sky

overview: Wright Construction Management served as construction manager for a 23,000-square-foot freezer addition to an active, USDA-regulated meat processing facility in the Chicago metro area.
The work expanded cold storage capacity while food production continued next door — the central constraint that shaped how the project was planned, sequenced, and turned over.

blocks.heading: Foundations and Site Work
paragraphs: The addition started below grade, with excavation, foundations, and a stone base built to carry the new freezer structure and its refrigerated floor.
WCM also oversaw environmental site assessment activities as part of the work.

items.alt: Formed concrete foundation walls and excavation at the freezer addition, with an excavator working in the background
Reinforcing steel set in a footing trench over the compacted stone base

blocks.alt: Structural steel frame and roof deck of the freezer addition partly clad in insulated metal panel, built directly against the existing plant
blocks.caption: The addition went up against the wall of a plant that never stopped running.

blocks.heading: The Refrigerated Floor
paragraphs: A freezer slab has to be kept from freezing the ground beneath it. The floor was built as a glycol-heated slab over floor insulation, with the glycol tubing run and pressure-tested before the pour.
The custom industrial ammonia refrigeration system tied into that floor — compressors, evaporators, control valves, and ammonia detection all integrated to hold temperature across the new space.

items.alt: Orange glycol tubing run in loops across the stone base inside the insulated metal panel shell, ahead of the heated slab pour
Two ride-on power trowels finishing the new concrete slab inside the freezer shell

blocks.heading: Solving the Site Constraint
paragraphs: The site had no room to spare. Rather than give up floor area to mechanical space, the design put the large evaporators in a refrigeration penthouse on the roof — preserving clear height and pallet positions inside the freezer.
That decision carried its own scope: a large external stair tower was built to give maintenance staff safe access up to the penthouse.

items.alt: Steel-framed refrigeration penthouse under construction on the roof of the freezer addition, with equipment set inside the frame
Galvanized external stair tower rising against the insulated metal panel wall beside an elevated condenser platform, with boom lifts working below

blocks.alt: Rows of steel equipment supports set on the new roof membrane at dusk, with the Chicago skyline on the horizon
blocks.caption: Roof-mounted equipment supports, with the city on the horizon.

blocks.heading: Building Inside an Operating USDA Plant
paragraphs: Working in an occupied facility meant close coordination with plant operations, multi-trade scheduling, and strict adherence to food safety protocols throughout.

WCM coordinated every trade on the job — excavation, concrete, insulated metal panel, refrigeration, electrical, structural steel, plumbing, roofing, and fire protection — and managed integration of the IMP building envelope and the fire protection system into the finished structure.

blocks.alt: Completed freezer interior with insulated metal panel walls, exposed steel framing, and a freshly finished floor slab
blocks.caption: The finished freezer, ready for racking.

gallery.alt: Pallet racking components staged on the finished freezer floor ahead of installation
Wide view of the completed freezer interior showing structural steel columns and the insulated panel end wall
Completed freezer addition from the yard, with the existing plant and process equipment alongside it

cta.heading: Adding cold storage to a running plant?
cta.sub: Book a 15-minute feasibility call and we'll walk the refrigeration, phasing, and food-safety constraints before they turn into change orders.
